name: Ephron
overview: The Scripture presents Ephron as the son of Zohar, a Hittite, who plays a significant role in the patriarchal narrative by selling Abraham the field containing the cave of Machpelah, a designated burial place. In Genesis 23, Ephron initially offers the land to Abraham as a gift but ultimately agrees to sell it for its full value in the presence of the community, underscoring the formal and honorable transaction. This account highlights Ephron’s position among the children of Heth and the respect Abraham shows by bowing before the people, reflecting the cultural and covenantal significance of securing a burial site. Additionally, Ephron is associated with a mountain on the boundary between the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, linking him geographically to the land promised to Abraham’s descendants.
